hyperedges.label: CloudIgniter API Request and Response Flow

nodes.label: Explicit Maintenance Execution
nodes.rationale: The installer must remain an explicit development or build-maintenance command because it modifies package.json and the workspace lockfile.

nodes.label: Identity Pool Role Bootstrap
nodes.rationale: The unauthorized role ARN is discovered only after the first deployment by listing identity pools or consulting amplify_outputs.json, then querying the pool roles.

nodes.label: Server Export Prohibition
nodes.rationale: The NextIntl plugin file is intended for next.config.ts and must not be exported from the server.

nodes.label: React-Powered Interactive Posts
nodes.rationale: MDX permits React and JSX to create interactive blog content such as clickable buttons.

nodes.label: Docusaurus Blog File Structure
nodes.rationale: Markdown files or folders in the blog directory become posts; folder-based posts conveniently co-locate their images, and dates may be inferred from filenames.

nodes.label: CloudIgniter API Call Strategy
nodes.rationale: A strict unified communication strategy provides consistent developer experience, predictable behavior, explicit contracts, type safety, observability, and low-boilerplate scaling.

nodes.label: Unified API Pattern
nodes.rationale: Committing to one pattern accelerates onboarding, improves maintainability, and prevents fragmentation and technical debt.

nodes.label: Backend-for-Frontend Pattern
nodes.rationale: Routing browser calls through local Next.js handlers keeps secrets and AWS details out of the browser and permits infrastructure refactoring without client changes.

nodes.label: POST with JSON Convention
nodes.rationale: Uniform POST requests with JSON bodies avoid accidental caching and sensitive query-string leakage while simplifying auditing and logging.

nodes.label: End-to-End API Flow
nodes.rationale: A single typed Request-to-Response model flowing through Next.js, AppSync, and Lambda removes ambiguity about transport, parsing, validation, and errors.

nodes.label: Single String Input Design
nodes.rationale: Transporting exactly one inputString avoids mapping templates and schema argument drift while retaining backend contract flexibility.

nodes.label: Normalized Error Handling
nodes.rationale: All failures use Response<T>, raw exceptions are not leaked, and each layer validates and normalizes errors to preserve a predictable contract.

nodes.label: Architecture Discipline as a Service
nodes.rationale: Strict API conventions improve stability, reduce regressions and onboarding time, and support scalable AWS integration for small teams.

nodes.label: GraphQL Errors versus Handler Errors
nodes.rationale: GraphQL/AppSync errors occupy the errors field, while handler-level structured errors live inside data as non-200 CloudIgniter Responses.

nodes.label: safeParseRequest()
nodes.rationale: Centralized non-throwing parsing converts inputString into Request<T> or null, ensuring malformed input becomes a structured error rather than a crash.

nodes.label: Environment Safety Guards
nodes.rationale: Handlers compare requested and runtime environments and reject dangerous live-environment operations before business logic runs.

nodes.label: Thin Handler Orchestration
nodes.rationale: Lambda handlers focus on validation and orchestration while shared server library functions own the business logic.

nodes.label: Critical Call Semantics
nodes.rationale: The critical flag distinguishes operations that should fail loudly or block progress from ordinary UI operations that may fail gracefully.

nodes.label: prepareApiRequest()
nodes.rationale: A centralized gatekeeper normalizes environment, authentication, AWS client configuration, and criticality before AppSync serialization.

nodes.label: Centralized AWS Client Configuration
nodes.rationale: Shared Cognito and DynamoDB client settings keep infrastructure details out of clients and route handlers while permitting explicit overrides.

nodes.label: API Reference as a Stable Contract
nodes.norm_label: api reference as a stable contract

nodes.label: Amazon Cognito User Pool Group Documentation
nodes.norm_label: amazon cognito user pool group documentation

nodes.label: Server-Prepared Runtime Context
nodes.rationale: The client Page treats config as immutable runtime truth prepared by the server, preventing client-side guessing or direct access to headers, cookies, and environment state.

nodes.label: Layered Authenticator Theme Merge
nodes.rationale: Amplify defaults, CloudIgniter base tokens, and minimal consumer overrides are layered in order to permit branding without sacrificing system consistency or upgrade compatibility.

nodes.label: Deterministic Authenticator Component Overrides
nodes.rationale: Nested props are deep-merged, but React component slots are replaced per key because deep-merging functions is unpredictable.

nodes.label: Authenticator UI and Cognito Backend Alignment
nodes.rationale: Visible sign-in and sign-up fields must match Cognito username, required attribute, and custom attribute settings or authentication flows may fail validation.
nodes.norm_label: authenticator ui and cognito backend alignment

nodes.label: Core and Extension Boundary
nodes.rationale: CloudIgniter-owned backend defaults remain in amplify while developer additions live in amplify_extended and are merged into the core resources.

nodes.label: Immutable Cognito Schema Decisions
nodes.rationale: Required attributes, sign-in methods, verification methods, and identifying user attributes generally cannot be changed after Cognito resources are configured.

nodes.label: Code-First Cloud Provisioning
nodes.rationale: Expressing data, business logic, authentication, and authorization in TypeScript lets Amplify provision AWS resources automatically and reduces manual service integration.

nodes.label: Upgrade-Safe Amplify Extension
nodes.rationale: Developers extend Amplify in amplify_extended rather than changing the core amplify folder so future CloudIgniter updates and upgrades remain possible.

nodes.label: Client Bundle Server-Module Fallbacks
nodes.rationale: Disabling fs and path fallbacks in client builds prevents server-only modules from leaking into browser bundles while retaining them for server code.

nodes.label: External Directory Support
nodes.rationale: Next.js externalDir support enables monorepo and linked local-package development scenarios.

nodes.label: CloudIgniter Boot Sequence
nodes.rationale: The startup pipeline orders framework setup, request-time localization, root configuration, route protection, client providers, and page rendering so each layer receives its prerequisites.

nodes.label: Client Provider Ordering
nodes.rationale: Amplify must initialize before authentication, authentication before route checks, and theme before UI paint; the error store remains available throughout.

nodes.label: Deep-Merge Message Assembly
nodes.rationale: System common, route namespace, custom common, and custom namespace dictionaries are merged into one request-specific message object.

nodes.label: Custom Message Overrides
nodes.rationale: Application dictionaries override system defaults cleanly while route namespaces keep translation payloads modular and small.

nodes.label: Hydration Warning Suppression
nodes.rationale: suppressHydrationWarning silences expected server/client markup differences such as those introduced by theme implementation.

nodes.label: Stylesheet Import Order
nodes.rationale: Loading library and authenticator styles through Kernel before globals.css guarantees that framework tokens and utilities precede application and page overrides.

nodes.label: Deterministic Theme Loading
nodes.rationale: Separating core, global, and authenticator CSS in a guaranteed order keeps SSR and CSR theming deterministic and avoids flashes of unstyled content.

nodes.label: Server and Client Page Separation
nodes.rationale: The Route Page handles request-time server orchestration and emits a serializable payload, while the colocated client wrapper owns UI composition, state, navigation, and event handling.

nodes.label: Unified Isomorphic Tracing
nodes.rationale: A single logging interface and canonical JSON-line format across browser and server environments makes traces predictable and analyzable for debugging, profiling, and auditing.

nodes.label: Canonical Trace Record Format
nodes.rationale: Every trace is represented as one JSON line with a strictly preserved field order so mixed client and server logs remain easy to parse and analyze.

nodes.label: Production Tracing Restraint
nodes.rationale: Tracing should remain disabled in production unless actively debugging, and logged payloads should be small and free of sensitive data to reduce overhead and exposure.

nodes.label: Page Client Wrapper
nodes.rationale: Centralizing page-shell composition and interactivity in a colocated Client Component provides consistent page structure and extensibility while isolating it from server-only logic.

nodes.label: Page Component
nodes.rationale: A single reusable client-side page shell centralizes scrolling, layout, chrome, internationalization hydration, loading, and instrumentation to guarantee predictable behavior across routes.

nodes.label: Route Page
nodes.rationale: The Route Page remains a thin Server Component that performs request-time orchestration and emits serializable configuration while delegating all interactive UI to its sibling client wrapper.

nodes.label: Environment Data Isolation
nodes.rationale: Separating production, test, and sandbox modes prevents fake data and destructive test features from contaminating production while enabling safe CRUD and deterministic cleanup.

nodes.label: Live Environment Guard
nodes.rationale: The backend rejects test and sandbox modes in live deployments, and test-only handlers must fail immediately unless the runtime mode explicitly permits them.

nodes.label: Environment-Aware Primary Key Scoping
nodes.rationale: The DynamoDB wrapper injects non-live environment suffixes into primary keys and includes envMode in reads and writes to prevent cross-environment contamination.

nodes.label: Safe Environment Operations
nodes.rationale: Production must use live mode, automated tests should use test, local experiments should use sandbox, and cleanup, seed data, and destructive features must never run against live records.

nodes.label: Move Fast Safely
nodes.rationale: Environment isolation, deterministic cleanup, and multi-tenant safeguards allow rapid development without risking production data.

nodes.label: Two-Layer Error Handling Model
nodes.rationale: Server boundaries provide predictable recovery for global crashes and loader failures, while the client store provides flexible UX for recoverable warnings and interactive notifications.

nodes.label: Stable Error IDs
nodes.rationale: Stable identifiers per error domain allow repeated conditions to update an existing error instead of creating duplicate notifications.

nodes.label: Severity-Driven Error UI
nodes.rationale: Critical failures block the session with a full-screen backdrop, while lower severities become sticky cards or dismissible modals.

nodes.label: Client Retry Separation
nodes.rationale: Client notifications emphasize visibility and user control rather than a universal retry contract because recovery is usually automatic or scenario-specific.

nodes.label: Segment Failure Isolation
nodes.rationale: Placing error.tsx within a route folder confines rendering failures to that segment, while global-error.tsx catches failures escaping all segment boundaries.

nodes.label: Error Boundary Limits
nodes.rationale: React boundaries catch render and streaming failures but not client event handlers, detached asynchronous work, API routes, middleware, not-found responses, or redirects.

nodes.label: Cloud Infrastructure and Ignition Brand Metaphor
nodes.norm_label: cloud infrastructure and ignition brand metaphor

nodes.label: Cloud Ignition Brand Metaphor
nodes.rationale: The mark combines a dark cloud outline with a vivid orange and yellow flame, visually expressing the CloudIgniter name as cloud technology being ignited.

nodes.label: Unavailable Brand Asset Metaphor
nodes.rationale: The broken cloud outline, scattered fragments, subdued flame, and question-like smoke communicate that a CloudIgniter logo or branded image is missing or unavailable.

nodes.label: Source Code Metaphor
nodes.rationale: A pair of opposing blue angle brackets serves as the conventional compact visual symbol for source code or developer-facing code content.

nodes.label: Layered API Separation
nodes.rationale: The architecture separates browser, Next.js server, and AWS cloud responsibilities so the client exchanges typed Request and Response envelopes without directly depending on AppSync, Lambda, or library implementation details.

nodes.label: Root HTML Element DOM Inspector Screenshot
nodes.norm_label: root html element dom inspector screenshot

nodes.label: Root Presentation State
nodes.rationale: The root html element exposes resolved theme, language, direction, and color-scheme state as attributes so browser rendering and CSS can consistently reflect the active presentation context.

nodes.label: Bilingual Locale Switching
nodes.rationale: The dropdown displays the active English locale with a checkmark while offering Arabic as an alternative, making the current language and available switch explicit.

nodes.label: Hydration Mismatch Suppression
nodes.rationale: Applying suppressHydrationWarning to the root html element suppresses warnings for expected server-client markup differences while locale, direction, fonts, and providers establish the application shell.

nodes.label: Kernel Base, Components, and Utilities CSS
nodes.norm_label: kernel base, components, and utilities css

nodes.label: Ordered CSS Composition
nodes.rationale: globals.css interleaves Tailwind base, component, and utility layers with the corresponding Kernel CSS layers to preserve a deliberate cascade order.

nodes.label: Application Extension over Kernel Defaults
nodes.rationale: The application Tailwind configuration imports and spreads the CloudIgniter Kernel configuration before adding application-specific theme extensions and plugins, preserving framework defaults while enabling customization.

nodes.label: Documentation Platform Brand Metaphor
nodes.rationale: The friendly green dinosaur holding a lined document visually combines the Docusaurus mascot with its role as a documentation-site platform.

nodes.label: React-Powered Documentation Experience
nodes.rationale: The illustration is explicitly titled Powered by React and combines a React emblem with the Docusaurus mascot, communicating that the documentation experience is built on React.

nodes.label: Content Focus
nodes.rationale: The explicit title Focus on What Matters and the prominent, uncluttered documentation page communicate that the documentation experience is designed to keep attention on essential content.
